summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after presenting with coffee ground emesis following dialysis, concerning for upper gastrointestinal bleeding. She had a history of nausea post-dialysis but no prior bleeding. Evaluation showed stable hemoglobin, minimal blood in the nasogastric tube, and no active bleeding, so endoscopy was deferred. She was managed conservatively with proton-pump inhibitors. During admission, she experienced severe nausea attributed to sodium thiosulfate, which was discontinued, leading to significant improvement. Her anion gap metabolic acidosis resolved after stopping the medication. Leukocytosis was present but cultures were negative; imaging showed no abscess, and wound flora were considered colonizers. Pain from calciphylaxis was managed with palliative care, including a fentanyl patch and oral hydromorphone. She developed transient diarrhea, which resolved without treatment. The patient was discharged to an extended care facility on optimized pain and dialysis regimens, with plans to reevaluate sodium thiosulfate dosing as an outpatient.
